dataset_metadata.disclaimer: New AI-generated English drafts of the recorded Classical Chinese; not scholarly reviewed. Original source interpretations are not verified geometry or modern etymology.

shuowen:4501.text: Qi calls grain-pounding 𦥭. Formed from 臼, with 屰 indicating the sound. Read like 膊.

shuowen:4502.text: To pound off wheat husks. Formed from 臼; 干 is what is used to pound into it.

shuowen:4503.text: To scoop from a mortar. Formed from 爪 and 臼. The Odes says: “Some winnow, some scoop.”

shuowen:4504.text: A small pitfall. Formed from 人 above 臼.

shuowen:4505.text: Evil or ill-omened. Depicts a hole in the ground, with crossing lines sunk inside it. All characters in this group follow 凶.

shuowen:4506.text: Disturbed with fear. Formed from 人 below 凶. The Spring and Autumn Commentary says: “The people of Cao were frightened.”

shuowen:4507.text: Separating hemp-stalk bark. Formed from 屮, with 八 depicting the bark and stalks of hemp. All characters in this group follow 朩. Read like 髕.

shuowen:4508.text: Hemp. Formed from 朩, with 台 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4509.text: A general name for flowers. The word 𣏟 conveys fineness: fine fibers accomplish the work. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 𣏟. The connection between flowers and fibers in the recorded text is uncertain.

shuowen:4510.text: A kind of hemp. Formed from 𣏟 and abbreviated 熒. The Odes says: “Over brocade, a hemp garment.”

shuowen:4511.text: To separate and disperse. Formed from 攴 and 𣏟; 𣏟 conveys separation and dispersal.

shuowen:4512.text: The same as 𣏟, processed by people under a roof. Formed from 广 and 𣏟. All characters in this group follow 麻.

shuowen:4513.text: Hemp thread not yet scoured and processed. Formed from 麻, with 後 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4514.text: Hemp stalks. Formed from 麻, with 取 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4515.text: A kind of 檾 hemp. Formed from 麻, with 俞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4516.text: Beans. Depicts beans growing. All characters in this group follow 尗.

shuowen:4517.text: To mix salt with beans and keep them in darkness, apparently for fermentation; the wording is uncertain. Formed from 尗, with 支 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4518.text: The top of a thing at its first growth. The upper part depicts growth, the lower its roots. All characters in this group follow 耑.

shuowen:4519.text: A vegetable name. Once planted, it lasts long, hence called 韭. Pictographic, above 一; 一 is the ground. This uses the same principle as 耑. All characters in this group follow 韭.

shuowen:4520.text: Minced vegetables, 齏. Formed from 韭, with 隊 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4521.text: To fall. Formed from 韭, with both 次 and 𠂔 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4522.text: A vegetable with chive-like leaves. Formed from 韭, with 㕢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4523.text: Mountain chives. Formed from 韭, with 㦰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4524.text: Small garlic. Formed from 韭, with 番 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4525.text: A gourd, 㼌. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 瓜.

shuowen:4526.text: A small gourd. Formed from 瓜, with 交 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4527.text: A small gourd, 㼎. Formed from 瓜, with 失 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Unbroken spread the gourds, large and small.”

shuowen:4528.text: A small gourd. Formed from 瓜, with abbreviated 熒 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4529.text: A gourd. Formed from 瓜, with abbreviated 繇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4530.text: The seeds inside a gourd. Formed from 瓜, with 辡 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4531.text: The root unable to support the top: weak and frail. Formed from two 瓜. Read like 庾.

shuowen:4532.text: A bottle gourd. Formed from 瓜, with 夸 indicating the sound. All characters in this group follow 瓠.

shuowen:4533.text: A gourd ladle. Formed from abbreviated 瓠, with 㶾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4534.text: A deep building covered by intersecting roof slopes. Pictographic. All characters in this group follow 宀.

shuowen:4535.text: A dwelling. Formed from 宀, with abbreviated 豭 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4536.text: A place to lodge or entrust oneself. Formed from 宀, with 乇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4537.text: Fullness or substance. Formed from 宀 and 至; 至 is where one stops.

shuowen:4538.text: The Son of Heaven’s Xuan chamber. Formed from 宀, with 𠄢 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4539.text: A north-facing window. Formed from 宀 and 口. The Odes says: “Block the north window and plaster the door.”

shuowen:4540.text: To nourish. The northeast corner of a room, where food is kept. Formed from 宀, with 𦣞 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4541.text: The sound of a door pivot; also the southeast corner of a room. Formed from 宀, with 㫐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4542.text: Recessed or sheltered, 宛: the southwest corner of a room. Formed from 宀, with 𢍏 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4543.text: To bend grass over oneself as a covering. Formed from 宀, with 夗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4544.text: A building’s eaves or roof. Formed from 宀, with 辰 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4545.text: The edge of a roof. Formed from 宀, with 于 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “A ridgepole above, eaves below.”

shuowen:4546.text: A large building. Formed from 宀, with 豐 indicating the sound. The Changes says: “Make his house grand.”

shuowen:4547.text: An enclosing wall. Formed from 宀, with 奐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4548.text: A building’s deep resonance. Formed from 宀, with 厷 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4549.text: A building’s resonance. Formed from 宀, with 弘 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4550.text: A building’s appearance. Formed from 宀, with 爲 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4551.text: A building spacious, 㝩㝗. Formed from 宀, with 康 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4552.text: Spacious, 㝩. Formed from 宀, with 良 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4553.text: What a building can hold. Formed from 宀, with 成 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4554.text: At peace. Formed from 宀, with 心 above 皿. People’s eating and drinking vessels are what put them at ease.

shuowen:4555.text: Settled or at peace. Formed from 宀 and 正.

shuowen:4556.text: To stop. Formed from 宀, with 是 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4557.text: Quiet. Formed from 女 beneath 宀.

shuowen:4558.text: At peace. Formed from 宀, with 必 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4559.text: Quiet. Formed from 宀, with 契 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4560.text: At peace. Formed from 宀, with 妟 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4561.text: Without human voices. Formed from 宀, with 尗 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4562.text: To examine or review, 覆. Formed from 宀 and 祭.

shuowen:4563.text: To arrive. Formed from 宀, with 親 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4564.text: Whole. Formed from 宀, with 元 indicating the sound. Ancient writing uses it for 寬.

shuowen:4565.text: Fully supplied. Another explanation: abundant. Formed from 宀, with 畐 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4566.text: Rich. Formed from 宀 and 貫; 貫 means valuable shells.

shuowen:4567.text: To store. Formed from 宀, with 𡥀 indicating the sound; 𡥀 is ancient-script 𠈃. The Book of Zhou says: “Display and store the red knife.”

shuowen:4568.text: To contain. Formed from 宀 and 谷.

shuowen:4569.text: Dispersed or idle. Formed from 宀, with a person under the roof, having no field work. The Book of Zhou says: “Those in the palace who eat without working.”

shuowen:4570.text: 𦤝𦤝, not seen. Another explanation: 𦤝𦤝, not seeing or attending to people. Formed from 宀, with 𦤝 indicating the sound. The repeated gloss is uncertain.

shuowen:4571.text: A treasure. Formed from 宀, 王 and 貝, with 缶 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4572.text: To live in a group. Formed from 宀, with 君 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4573.text: To serve in office. Formed from 宀 and 臣.

shuowen:4574.text: A convicted person serving within a building. Formed from 宀 and 辛; 辛 means crime.

shuowen:4575.text: To hold an official post. Formed from 宀 and 寸: one attending to government offices. It uses 寸, meaning rules and measures.

shuowen:4576.text: To dwell in honor. Formed from 宀, with 龍 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4577.text: Lenient. Formed from 宀, with 有 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4578.text: Where one is at ease. Formed beneath 宀 and above 一, with abbreviated 多 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4579.text: To put things down. Formed from 宀, with 舄 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4580.text: Night. Formed from 宀, because beneath the roof it is dark, with 肖 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4581.text: To stay. Formed from 宀, with 𠈇 indicating the sound; 𠈇 is ancient-script 夙.

shuowen:4582.text: To lie down. Formed from 宀, with 钅 recorded as indicating the sound; the trailing 鲞 in the source is unexplained and the analysis uncertain.

shuowen:4583.text: Darkness closing in. Formed from 宀, with 丏 indicating the sound. Read like 眄 in the Book of Zhou’s “If medicine does not cause dizziness.”

shuowen:4584.text: A building broad and spacious. Formed from 宀, with 萈 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4585.text: To awaken. Formed from 宀, with 吾 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4586.text: To move quickly in one’s dwelling. Formed from 宀, with 疌 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4587.text: Few. Formed from 宀 and 頒; 頒 means dividing and distributing, hence few.

shuowen:4588.text: To lodge temporarily. Formed from 宀, with 各 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4589.text: To entrust or lodge. Formed from 宀, with 奇 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4590.text: To lodge temporarily. Formed from 宀, with 禺 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4591.text: To dwell without ritual furnishings. Formed from 宀, with 婁 indicating the sound; the meaning of 無禮居 is uncertain.

shuowen:4592.text: Poor and afflicted. Formed from 宀, with 久 indicating the sound. The Odes says: “Alone and helpless in poverty.”

shuowen:4593.text: Freezing. Formed from a person under 宀, covered and cushioned with 茻, with 仌 below.

shuowen:4594.text: To injure. Formed from 宀 and 口: speech starts from the household. 丯 indicates the sound.

shuowen:4595.text: To enter a house and search. Formed from 宀, with 索 indicating the sound.

shuowen:4596.text: Exhausted or at an end. Formed from 宀, with 𥱩 indicating the sound; 𥱩 is the same as 𥷤.

shuowen:4597.text: Wickedness. Outside it is 盜; inside, 宄. Formed from 宀, with 九 indicating the sound. Read like 軌.

shuowen:4598.text: To block off. Formed from 宀, with 𠭥 indicating the sound. Read like 㝮 in the Book of Yu’s “Expel the Three Miao.”

shuowen:4599.text: To pass beyond. Another explanation: a cave dwelling. Formed from 宀, with abbreviated 碭 indicating the sound. Xiang in Runan has Dang Township.

shuowen:4600.text: To dwell. Formed from 宀 and 木. Read like 送.
